sources.section: Build your own Emulator / Virtual Machine

summary.title: GameBoy Emulation in JavaScript
summary.one_liner: A multi-part series showing how to build a GameBoy emulator in JavaScript, covering the CPU, memory, GPU timing, graphics, input, sprites, interrupts, memory banking and timers.
takeaways: How to emulate a CPU in JavaScript as the starting point for a GameBoy emulator core
How the GameBoy memory map is mapped onto the CPU address bus and loading ROM images asynchronously
How to synchronise CPU and graphics timing and render output to an HTML5 canvas
How keypad input, sprites, interrupts (including vertical blanking), memory banking and timers are implemented in an emulator
summary.summary: This is an index page for a nine-part series by Imran Nazar (2010–2011) on building a GameBoy emulator in JavaScript, presented as an argument that JavaScript is a general-purpose, Turing-complete language. Each listed part covers one subsystem: the CPU, memory, GPU timings, graphics, integration, input, sprites, interrupts, memory banking and timers. The articles are written as step-by-step explanations of the hardware and how it is simulated in code, with a working demo introduced in part five. The page text shown here is only the list of article summaries, so the depth of individual parts is not visible from this page.
